description: deixis N[T] attachment vectors — exact fresh attachment, ADR 0009 §8. attach(A,p,k,B) is defined exactly when p ∈ D_A and p ++ [k] ∉ D_A (E2 availability), and then D_C = D_A ∪ {r ++ q | q ∈ D_B} (E0) and v_C = v_A ∪ {r ++ q ↦ v_B(q)} (E1), with r = p ++ [k]. Hand-authored from docs/design/0009-optional-node-values.md alone, per vectors/NODE-PLAN.md; not generated by an implementation, and replayed against the four cores by tools/conformance/harness.mjs. Spelling as in NODE-PLAN.md. A defined result is the WHOLE resulting tree, compared with the structural equality of node-identity.json, so an extra, missing or moved position anywhere makes the case fail. `attach-commute` attaches `first` then `second`, and separately `second` then `first`; both results must equal `expected`. Under ADR 0010 this file reads as the explicit optional instantiation Node[Option[fixture]], with the tag-respecting option slot of vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md; every case here holds there under the mandatory core's generic laws (checked case by case on 2026-09-23; see NODE-PLAN.md).

cases.name: attach-at-valued-root
cases.note: X11/C6. §8: N admits attachment at every existing node, and E2 makes it defined whenever the preconditions hold. The root is valued AND has no children, the old model's Leaf(t) exactly (E, §10.1); attaching under it is the decisive difference. Refusing here is the old-model behaviour.

cases.name: attach-keeps-parent-value-with-existing-children
cases.note: C1. E1: v_C ⊇ v_A, so the parent's Some(7) stays at ε. An implementation that rebuilds the parent from its children alone drops it (§6: children cannot reveal an independent own value).

cases.name: attach-does-not-relocate-or-add-a-value-slot
cases.note: C2/C5. The result has exactly two positions (E0), with Some(7) still at ε. The rejected workaround of §1, which moves the parent's value under a new head child, would give three positions and a value at a different address.

cases.name: attach-at-deep-valued-parent
cases.note: X11. Attachment below a valued interior node at depth one. The parent keeps Some(a) and its old child; the ancestor context (the unvalued root) is rebuilt unchanged (§8 local reconstruction).

cases.name: attach-empty-subtree-adds-exactly-one-position
cases.note: X10. E0 with D_B = {ε}: exactly one new path, [k], and no new value. An implementation that treats an empty subtree as nothing to insert returns the input unchanged, which §8 names as insufficient.

cases.name: attach-subtree-with-descendants
cases.note: E0/E1 with a non-trivial B: every path q of B appears at r ++ q with its own value. at(C, r) ≡ B (§8 consequences).

cases.name: attach-occupied-key-refuses
cases.note: C7. §8 precondition r ∉ D_A: undefined when the child key is occupied. Overwriting the existing child (losing Some(a)) is the failure this catches.

cases.name: attach-occupied-key-refuses-even-when-identical
cases.note: C7. The precondition is about the KEY, not the content. The existing and offered subtrees are ≡, and it is still undefined: attach is not an idempotent upsert.

cases.name: attach-missing-parent-refuses
cases.note: §8 precondition p ∈ D_A: undefined when the parent is missing. Creating the missing parent on the way is C10's auto-vivification, one operation over.

cases.name: attach-empty-key-is-fresh-beside-zero-byte-key
cases.note: X5. The empty key is fresh although the key 00 exists: they are different byte strings.

cases.name: attach-empty-key-occupied-refuses
cases.note: X5/C7. The empty key occupies its slot like any other key.

cases.name: attach-leaves-siblings-values-and-absence-unchanged
cases.note: C9. §8: attachment retains every old value AND absence and introduces no unrelated changes. The unvalued sibling 6a stays unvalued and childless, and the valued sibling 6c keeps its value and its child: restrict(C, D_A) ≡ A.

cases.name: attach-keeps-payload-opaque
cases.note: C8. Payload class strings that look like the option tags stay opaque Some values through attachment (§2: T is opaque).

cases.name: attach-commute-at-root
cases.note: X13. §8: attach(attach(n,p,k,a),p,j,b) ≡ attach(attach(n,p,j,b),p,k,a) for distinct fresh k, j. Independent additions commute because their new domains are disjoint.

cases.name: attach-commute-below-valued-node
cases.note: X13/X11/X5. Commutation below a valued node, with the empty key and a non-UTF-8 key as the two fresh keys. Either order gives the same tree, and the parent keeps Some(a) in both.
